title: Two discounts do not add
hook: 20% off, then 10% off: is that a 30% price cut?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Calculate sequential discounts from the reduced base.

objective: Calculate sequential discounts from the reduced base.

claims.text: A applies 20% off and then 10% off the reduced price. B applies 30% off once. Scaled model; fictional offers; no other fees.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Original=100€, A=€72 and B=€70. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.8,0.9]; B=["*","x",0.7]; x denotes Original. At x=100, A=72, B=70; recall at x=115: B=80.5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: The second percentage acts on what remains. Multiplying 0.8 by 0.9 leaves 0.72 of the original price, not 0.70. The changed base explains the gap on the receipts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*","x",0.8,0.9]; B=["*","x",0.7]; x denotes Original. claims.text: A applies 20% off and then 10% off the reduced price. B applies 30% off once. Change only Original to 115€. What is B (30%-off) now? Correct: €80.5. Use B's stated rule with Original=115€: it gives €80.5. The second percentage acts on what remains. Multiplying 0.8 by 0.9 leaves 0.72 of the original price, not 0.70. The changed base explains the gap on the receipts.

recall.question: A applies 20% off and then 10% off the reduced price. B applies 30% off once. Change only Original to 115€. What is B (30%-off) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Original=115€: it gives €80.5. The second percentage acts on what remains. Multiplying 0.8 by 0.9 leaves 0.72 of the original price, not 0.70. The changed base explains the gap on the receipts.

safety.assumptions: A applies 20% off and then 10% off the reduced price. B applies 30% off once.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
